newsitem.title: CANADA: BCE unit launches India cell phone network.
newsitem.headline: BCE unit launches India cell phone network.

text.p: BCE Inc unit Bell Canada International (BCI) said on Thursday that it launched with its partner Tata Group a cellular telephone network in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh.

Operating under the name Tata Communications, the new company is licenced to serve the nearly 70 million residents, 850 large-scale enterprises and 100,000 small businesses in India's fifth-largest state, BCI said.
As stipulated under Indian foreign ownership rules, 51 percent of the equity in the cellular and basic telephone companies is held by the Tata Group, BCI said.
Tata Group is India's largest business house. BCI owns 39 percent of the cellular and basic telephone companies. American International Group Inc holds the remaining 10 percent of each company.
BCE is providing managerial and technical support, including the first chief executive officers for both companies, BCI said.
Richard French, chief executive at Tata Communications, said the company will be offering long distance and a full range of options and features within the next three weeks.

BCI, which is responsible for BCE's foreign network operations, also has cellular operations in Colombia and China and cable licences in Brazil. It also holds a stake in newly formed British telephony company Cable & Wireless Communications.
